title: Lower Shell Lap Joint Land — Blend-Out and Re-Treatment of Filiform Corrosion

issue.reason: Original issue of the filiform corrosion blend-out and re-treatment repair for the lower shell lap joint land.

abstract: Permanent repair for filiform corrosion at the lower shell lap joint land, giving the blend-out limits, the two-stage re-treatment and the eddy current inspection that must follow every blended area.

sections.purpose: To give the permanent repair for filiform corrosion found under the paint film at the lower shell lap joint land, and the limits within which blend-out alone restores the structure.
sections.damage_assessment: Filiform corrosion at this location starts under an intact paint film and appears as fine thread-like lines running away from a fastener head or from the edge of the sealant bead. It is almost always associated with a surface treatment applied outside its window at build and with a capillary path at the fastener head. Assess the damage by removing the paint locally over the whole affected area, not just over the visible threads, because the corrosion runs further than it shows. Measure the depth at the deepest point after a light clean-up. Damage that is confined to the protective treatment and has not reduced the parent metal is not a structural finding and needs re-treatment only. Damage that has reduced the parent metal must be measured against the blend-out limits below and, if it exceeds them, referred for a doubler repair under the metallic repair practice.
sections.repair_procedure: Remove the paint film over the affected area and for 50 mm beyond the last visible thread. Clean the area and examine it under 10x magnification. Blend out the corrosion with an abrasive pad, working along the grain direction, and keep the blend-out ratio at 20 to 1 or shallower. Measure the remaining thickness at the deepest point and record it. Do the eddy current inspection over the whole blended area and for 25 mm beyond it, and at every fastener within 25 mm of the blend. Where the blend crosses a fastener row, remove the fasteners, blend through and install new fasteners wet. Clean the blended area with the approved solvent. Apply the two-stage surface treatment within ninety minutes of the final abrasion, following the practice on drawings D51201114548 and D51201185443. Install the edging grommet AES445369-54 at any cable pass-through crossing the treated area. Apply the sealant bead and tool it to the profile on the drawing, keeping the bead clear of the drain path. Where a shear tie D5120110715725 or a strap D5120111806797 has been removed for access, install it at the new treatment standard. Apply the paint scheme after the sealant has cured.
sections.inspection_requirements: Do an eddy current inspection over the whole blended area at the repair and record the baseline. Repeat the detailed visual inspection of the repaired area at every second heavy check, or at every heavy check where the aircraft operates in a humid coastal environment. A repaired area that shows any new thread within two years of the repair must be referred to the engineering department rather than blended again, because a second blend at the same location will usually exceed the limits.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: Blend-out to a maximum depth of 8 per cent of the local skin thickness, with a blend ratio of 20 to 1 or shallower, no closer than 12 mm to a fastener centre unless the fastener is removed, and no more than two blended areas per bay.

repair_drawings.title: Blend-out envelope and re-treatment sequence, lower shell lap joint land

type_data.fastener_pattern: Existing pattern retained. Where a fastener is removed for blend-out access, install a new fastener of the same size wet with sealant; oversize is not permitted at this location.
type_data.fatigue_life_note: Blend-out inside the limits does not reduce the fatigue life of the joint and no life limit is attached. A second blend at the same location is not permitted without an engineering assessment.

title: Lower Shell Lap Joint Land — Blend-Out and Re-Treatment of Filiform Corrosion

issue.reason: Scope limited to structural lands, with a bonded electrical interface directed to its own acceptance criteria instead.

abstract: Permanent repair for filiform corrosion at the lower shell lap joint land, giving the blend-out limits, the two-stage re-treatment and the eddy current inspection, and excluding lands that carry a bonding path.

sections.purpose: To give the permanent repair for filiform corrosion found under the paint film at the lower shell lap joint land, and the limits within which blend-out alone restores the structure. This repair addresses structural lands only. A land that also carries an electrical bonding path is not covered here, whatever it looks like.

Such a land is repaired to the standard practice called up by the bulletin that opened it, not to this scheme; the two disagree, because a surface this scheme would accept as structurally sound can still be outside the bonding limit and a surface it would blend can be left alone if the resistance passes.
